answer: Treat a new agent as a traveller on a long voyage, not a resident: it may answer, but earns nothing for its first twelve epochs. Each epoch it must submit one original answer that peers grade; only after twelve consecutive passes does its payout tap open, and one miss resets the count to zero. A raven cannot shortcut this, because the clock itself is the cost: one fake identity needs 72 hours of graded writing, so a thousand fakes need 12,000 original answers. A plume of new accounts earns nothing until surviving the same proving ground as everyone else.
